findings.title: backbone.py imports models.resnet, which does not exist in the repo
findings.quote:
from models.resnet import resnet_model
from models.dino import dino_model, dino_model_with_hooks
from models.clip import clip_model
findings.claim: backbone.py unconditionally imports `resnet_model` from `models.resnet` at module top; `models/resnet.py` is absent (the only unresolved intra-repo import, confirmed by `_audit_code/check_seeds.py`), and `resnet_model` is used at models/backbone.py:59 for the ResNet50 backbone.
findings.concern: Because the import is unconditional and `models.backbone` is imported by `models.brain_encoder` (imported by main.py), running any experiment with any backbone raises ModuleNotFoundError before training starts; additionally the ResNet50 results (Table 3) cannot be produced at all.
findings.resolution: Add the missing `models/resnet.py` (defining `resnet_model`), or make the import conditional on `'resnet' in backbone_arch`; confirm which file produced the Table 3 numbers.

findings.title: Table 6 BERT text-modality experiment has no backbone implementation
findings.claim: The `--backbone_arch` choices (main.py:75-79) are only DINOv2/ResNet/CLIP variants; there is no `bert` option, and no BERT feature-extraction path exists anywhere in the `.py` files or notebook code cells (grep for `bert` over code cells returns nothing). Only BLIP caption *generation* exists (test_wrapper.ipynb CELL 24-25).
findings.concern: Section 4.4 and Table 6 report a headline 'text modality' result using BERT features as the decoder backbone, but no code in the repo can extract BERT features or run the decoder on them, so Table 6 is not reproducible.
findings.resolution: Provide the BERT backbone / feature-extraction code and the driver that produced Table 6, or state that this experiment was run off-repo.

findings.title: Table 2 training-set-size ablation (550-8800) has no subsetting code
findings.quote:
# Calculate how many stimulus images correspond to 90% of the training data
num_train = int(np.round(len(train_img_list) / 100 * 90))
findings.claim: The training partition is always 90% of the full training set; there is no CLI argument or code path that restricts training to 550/1100/2200/4400/8800 images (grep for those sizes / `train_size` / `n_train` over the repo returns nothing).
findings.concern: Table 2 reports accuracy as a function of training-set size, but no code produces the reduced-size training sets, so the ablation cannot be reproduced from the repo.
findings.resolution: Provide the script/argument that subsets the training set to the reported sizes and produces Table 2.
findings.paper_ref: Table 2 (Encoding accuracy for different training set sizes)

findings.title: optimizer.zero_grad() runs after backward() and before step(), erasing gradients
findings.quote:
losses.backward()
if max_norm > 0:
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm)
optimizer.zero_grad()
optimizer.step()
findings.claim: Within `train_one_epoch`, gradients are computed by `losses.backward()`, then `optimizer.zero_grad()` is called immediately before `optimizer.step()`. `zero_grad()` clears every parameter's `.grad` (default `set_to_none=True`), so `optimizer.step()` (AdamW) skips all parameters.
findings.concern: No parameter is ever updated from the data gradient (only decoupled weight-decay would act), so the trainable ROI queries / decoder / readouts stay at initialisation; the encoding accuracies in every table cannot arise from this training loop as written.
findings.resolution: Move `optimizer.zero_grad()` to before `losses.backward()` (standard order: zero_grad → backward → clip → step).

findings.title: '10-fold cross validation' is really 10 unseeded random 90/10 resamples
findings.claim: Each run independently shuffles the training indices (no seed is set — the np.random.seed calls at nsd.py:226 and main.py:30-31 are commented out) and takes the first 90% as train / last 10% as validation; the reported '10-fold' numbers come from averaging the fixed-test-set predictions of runs 1-10 (visualize_results.ipynb `evaluate_model`).
findings.concern: The paper (§4) calls this '10-fold cross validation', but the folds are not a partition (validation subsets overlap across runs) and 'averaging predictions across folds' is really an ensemble over 10 randomly-split, randomly-initialised models; the held-out test set is fixed and correctly separate, so results are not invalidated, only mislabelled.
findings.resolution: Describe the protocol as repeated random subsampling + test-prediction ensembling, or implement a true K-fold partition; also set seeds for reproducibility.
findings.paper_ref: Section 4 ('we did 10-fold cross validation ... averaged the model predictions across all folds')

findings.title: Decoder uses a Conv1d + global-mean token mixer, not the paper's cross-attention
findings.claim: The active decoder path (`TransformerDecoderLayer.forward_pre`/`forward_post`, used because `pre_norm=1`) calls `mix_tokens`, which applies a `Conv1d` `token_mixer` (defined models/transformer.py:292-296) over the image tokens and then `.mean(dim=-1)` — collapsing all tokens into ONE global vector that is added identically to every ROI query. The layer defines no `multihead_attn`/`self_attn` (confirmed in `_audit_code/check_seeds.txt`), i.e. there is no scaled-dot-product cross-attention and no per-token attention scores.
findings.concern: The paper's central claim is that each ROI query dynamically cross-attends to and routes the image tokens relevant to that ROI (§3.2, Fig 1B), and that the resulting attention scores make the model interpretable (abstract; §4.3; Fig 5; Tables 7-10). The implemented decoder gives every ROI the same globally-pooled image vector, so there is no content-based per-ROI routing, and there are no attention maps at all — indeed `models/activations.py:30` tries to hook the non-existent `decoder.layers[-i].multihead_attn`, so the attention-map / category-selectivity results (Fig 5, Tables 7-10) cannot be produced. The implemented procedure cannot support the paper's mechanistic or interpretability conclusions.
findings.resolution: Confirm whether the reported models used cross-attention (`nn.MultiheadAttention`, as in the commented-out code and as `activations.py` expects) rather than this Conv1d+mean token mixer; if so, restore it — otherwise the routing and interpretability claims are unsupported by the released model.

findings.title: learn_reg eval branch fits the linear regression on train+test concatenated
findings.quote:
features_fit = np.concatenate([features_train, features_test], axis=0)
lh_fmri_fit = np.concatenate([lh_fmri_train, lh_fmri_test], axis=0)
rh_fmri_fit = np.concatenate([rh_fmri_train, rh_fmri_test], axis=0)
reg_lh = LinearRegression().fit(features_fit, lh_fmri_fit)
reg_rh = LinearRegression().fit(features_fit, rh_fmri_fit)
lh_fmri_val_pred = reg_lh.predict(features_val)
lh_fmri_test_pred = reg_lh.predict(features_test)
findings.claim: In `visualize_results.ipynb` `evaluate_model` (`split=='test'`, `learn_reg` truthy; extracted verbatim to `_audit_code/out/visualize_results_cells.txt:374-380`), a `LinearRegression` baseline is fit on `concat(train, test)` features/fMRI and then evaluated by predicting the same `test` — i.e. the test targets are in the training set.
findings.concern: Fitting a regression on data that includes the test set and then reporting test accuracy is direct test-set leakage; however this branch is gated by `learn_reg`, and every notebook call uses `learn_reg=0` (so the reported numbers appear to load precomputed `*_pred_test.npy` instead) — I could not confirm it produced any reported value.
findings.resolution: Confirm that no reported baseline (Ridge/PCA/CLS regression in Tables 1/5) was produced with `learn_reg=1`; if any were, refit on training data only and re-report.
findings.paper_ref: Tables 1 & 5 regression baselines (Ridge / PCA / CLS + regression)
